description: Two side-by-side TEM micrographs of deformed Fe–25% Al, imaged near the [0 0 1] zone axis with the imaging g vector parallel to 1 0 0 (indicated by the white arrow in the lower-right of the right image). Left panel (dark field, 1 0 0 beam at the Bragg condition): a heavily mottled, speckled bright background crossed by long, strongly curved dark dislocation lines that sweep in large arcs; the labels 't' (twice) mark thermal APBs from coarse B2 domains and 's' (twice) mark APBI faults; the fine background speckling is attributed to fine DO3 domains or partial disorder. Right panel (weak beam, 2 0 0 beam with approximately the 4 0 0 beam excited): dark matrix carrying many short, fine bright dislocation segments, largely straight and near-parallel, arranged in bands close to the screw orientation, with loosely coupled pairs; 's' appears twice; a black scale-bar box in the lower right is labelled 0.2µm. Read together, the pair demonstrates that loosely coupled (1/2)1 1 1 superpartials separated by weak APB faults are resolved in both imaging modes, i.e. APB energies are too low to keep them closely coupled.

observations.observation: The left panel is a dark-field TEM micrograph with a strongly mottled, speckled bright background crossed by long curved dark dislocation lines; the letters 't' and 's' each appear twice as annotations.

The right panel is a weak-beam TEM micrograph with a dark matrix carrying many short, fine bright dislocation segments that are largely straight and near-parallel, with the letter 's' appearing twice.
A black scale bar inside a box in the lower-right corner of the right panel is labelled 0.2µm.
A white arrow in the lower-right of the right panel marks the imaging g vector direction (pointing up and to the right).

Dislocation lines in the left (dark field) panel are long and strongly curved, whereas the resolved segments in the right (weak beam) panel are shorter and nearly straight, consistent with the reported predominance of near-screw orientations.
The caption states the zone axis is near [0 0 1] and the imaging g vector is parallel to 1 0 0 for both images, as shown by the arrow.

The caption states the dark field image was obtained with the 1 0 0 beam at the Bragg condition and the weak beam image with the 2 0 0 beam while approximately the 4 0 0 beam was excited, to give fine dislocation contrast plus residual APB contrast.

The caption states that in dark field the 't' marks denote a few thermal APBs from the coarse B2 domains, and that the background speckling may be due to fine DO3 domains or formation of some disorder (composition near the two-phase disorder + DO3 regime).
The caption states that the faults marked 's' are APBI faults produced by movement of (1/2)1 1 1 dislocations (B2 convention).

The caption states that comparison of the dark field and weak beam images shows such dislocations initiate or terminate APBI faults when arranged in pairs (B2 superdislocations) or as four-coupled dislocations (DO3 superdislocations).

The citing text asserts that various pairs of loosely coupled dislocations connected by an APB can be distinguished in both the dark field and weak beam images of this figure, because the APBI and APBII energies are insufficiently high to retain dislocations together as closely coupled superdislocations.
The citing text asserts that despite being loosely coupled by weak APB faults, these dislocations largely glide and behave as individual (1/2)1 1 1 dislocations in the DO3-ordered Fe–25% Al alloy.

subfigures.description: Dark-field TEM micrograph (1 0 0 beam, Bragg condition) of deformed Fe–25% Al showing a mottled, speckled bright background crossed by long curved dark dislocation lines; labels 't' (thermal APB, twice) and 's' (APBI fault, twice) are set on the image.

Weak-beam TEM micrograph (2 0 0 beam, ~4 0 0 excited) showing dark background with numerous fine, short, nearly straight bright dislocation segments in near-screw orientation, loosely coupled pairs, two 's' labels, a white arrow marking g and a black scale bar labelled 0.2µm at lower right.

unreadable_items: left panel, top-left corner: a dark curved band/large defect is only partially resolved and carries no label
the fine background speckle in the left panel cannot be assigned unambiguously to DO3 domains versus disorder from the pixels alone
